thread:
sara-oncall: paging the team 3: alert from runtime: multiple pods hitting CUDA OOM during prefill on pool-inference-7, containers restarting, spike in 5xx for generation endpoints. flagging P1. @miguel-infra @ashley-runtime please triage
ops-bot: INCIDENT CREATED  ID: INC-2026-03-15-2790019000  Severity: 1  Rule: runtime.prefill.cuda_oom > 2/min  Affected: pool-inference-7, gpu-node-12
sara-oncall: quick paste of the top error from pod logs: `E runtime.prefill: cudaMalloc returned 0x2 (out of memory) allocating 17.9G for kv_cache` and then `OOMKilled` from kube. lots of long-context clients hitting the beta/long route.
miguel-infra: running a quick `kubectl get pods -o wide` and `kubectl describe node gpu-node-12` now. cordoning node gpu-node-12 to limit blast radius.
michael-sre: are we certain it's workload and not a driver/firmware regression?
miguel-infra: checked driver version and dmesg. no ECC or hardware errors. GPU memory baseline normal when idle. pattern lines up with prefill allocation bursts.
ashley-runtime: we rolled out `beta-long` max_context=300k yesterday to experiment  looks like KV cache allocations are scaling linearly and exceeding expected model footprint for some vendor models. Immediate plan: 1) hotpatch runtime to enable `prefill.memory_throttle=true` which will reject or queue prefill requests exceeding a dynamic per-model cap, 2) rollback the 300k setting to 64k for beta-long while we analyze.
sara-oncall: can you push the hotpatch with canary? we need to reduce customer impact fast.
ops-bot: DEPLOY REQUEST  Change: runtime.flag.prefill_memory_throttle=true  Approvers: ashley-runtime, miguel-infra
ashley-runtime: approving. starting canary `deploy-bot rollout start runtime-hotpatch-prefill-throttle --canary=3`
deploy-bot: ROLLOUT STARTED  runtime-hotpatch-prefill-throttle  canary: 3 pods  image: runtime:v3.2.2-hotfix-prefill
miguel-infra: cordoned gpu-node-12, evicting non-critical inference pods. temporarily tainting nodes with `prefill-heavy=true:NoSchedule` and updating routing to avoid sending long prefill traffic to non-dedicated pools. Also scaling pool-inference-7 up by 50% for capacity headroom. command: `kubectl scale deployment/pool-inference-7 --replicas=9`
emily-cs: customers reporting 502/503s. I'm sending initial briefing now: "Were investigating elevated error rates affecting some generation requests. Engineers are mitigating; we will update within 30 minutes."
michael-sre: monitoring: raising alert sensitivity so we see any regressions immediately. added a short-term dedupe window to reduce pager spam while we triage.
ashley-runtime: canary metrics after 5m: prefill rejection rate ~1.5% (we're rejecting the extreme requests instead of OOMing), memory stable on canaries. promoting. `deploy-bot rollout promote runtime-hotpatch-prefill-throttle`
deploy-bot: ROLLOUT PROMOTED  runtime-hotpatch-prefill-throttle  status: in-progress  target: 9 pods
miguel-infra: rolling back the beta-long max_context: `route update beta-long --max_context=65536 --reason="mitigate OOMs"`
sara-oncall: any risk to correctness from throttling / rejecting prefills? will SDKs retry?
ashley-runtime: SDKs will surface a retriable 429 when auto-slicing is available; for now we return 413/429 depending on the policy. we'll add guidance to the error body recommending chunking or lower context. adding a debug log sample to help customers: 
```
{
  "error": "prefill_exceeds_model_cap",
  "recommended_max_tokens": 65536,
  "retryable": true
}
```
emily-cs: updating customer note: added explicit guidance to reduce context and enabling SDK auto-slicing for affected customers where available. sent update at 10:31 UTC.
michael-sre: observed a node-flap pattern: kubelet restarted containers on gpu-node-12 twice within 6m, likely due to repeated OOMs causing system instability. we've scheduled that node for extended isolation until end of investigation.
miguel-infra: new observation from logs: older model variants (v1.*) use a different KV layout and are allocating unexpectedly large staging buffers during tokenization; filing a ticket to audit model adapters. for immediate safety Ive added a kill-signal handler to favor graceful reject over restart when memory pressure detected.
sara-oncall: summarize mitigations so I can put in incident notes: 1) cordon/taint gpu-node-12, 2) scale up pool and route heavy prefill to dedicated capacity, 3) deploy runtime hotpatch to throttle prefill memory and reject extreme requests, 4) rollback beta-long max_context, 5) customer advisory sent. anything missing?
ashley-runtime: added: replace model variant for incoming long-context traffic with quantized model that uses ~40% less VRAM. that's already live for the canary.
michael-sre: I'm taking over the rotation in 20 minutes. request: follow-up actions to include: long-term KV cap by model, model-adapter memory audit, SDK auto-slicing/streaming, and a guardrail that rejects requests which would push expected allocation past a safety margin.
sara-oncall: go ahead and create the postmortem skeleton. ops-bot can you do that?
ops-bot: POSTMORTEM CREATED  INC-2026-03-15-2790019000  Owner: ashley-runtime  Template: runtime-prefill-oom Visibility: private
emily-cs: customer update sent at 10:48 UTC with follow-up ETA TBD. asking for list of impacted customers so we can target higher-touch outreach.
miguel-infra: temporary telemetry note: added a dashboard showing `prefill.kv_alloc_gb` per route and `prefill.rejected_count` so we can correlate. also set a short-lived alert: prefill.rejected_count > 5/min to catch throttling backpressure.
nashley-runtime: creating follow-up tasks: TASK-#1 enforce KV caps per model profile; TASK-#2 add prefill memory guardrail to runtime; TASK-#3 SDK client retries/auto-slice. linking tasks to postmortem.
michael-sre: handoff acceptance: I'll monitor the OOM rate and node health for next 12 hours, coordinate with infra to bring gpu-node-12 back only after extended soak testing. leaving a watch checklist: 1) OOM rate < 0.5/min for 30m, 2) no new node flaps, 3) confirm autoscaler does not place prefill-heavy pods on small GPUs.
sara-oncall: thanks. marking incident as "mitigated" when OOM rate below threshold for 30m and no container restarts on tainted nodes.
(11:12 UTC) michael-sre: OOM rate down to 0.2/min fleet-wide, no restarts observed for 35m. marking mitigated and adding postmortem owner to follow-up.
sara-oncall: closing the live incident channel; follow-ups and RCA in postmortem. great work everyone. :clap:
